# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 25 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 1QHa (Cave 1), Col. 25 | **Condition:** very fragmentary

---

**1** [...] for [...] my heart [...] has trembled at Your judgments [...]

**2** [...] and my inner being is undone, and my bones are broken apart [...]

**3** [...] and my heart pours out like water, and my flesh melts like wax [...]

**4** [...] and my knees buckle like water spilled upon a slope [...]

**5** [...] and I said: In my transgression I am forsaken [...]

**6** [...] from Your covenant. But when I recalled the power of Your hand [...]

**7** [...] together with the abundance of Your mercies, I stood upright and rose [...]

**8** [...] and my spirit held fast to its station, for I relied [...]

**9** [...] upon Your covenant faithfulness, and the abundance of Your mercies [...]

**10** [...] for You atone for transgression, and You cleanse a person from guilt through Your righteousness [...]

**11** [...] and [...] my strength [...] has faltered before Your glory [...]

**12** [...] and there is no remnant, and no strength [...] remains in me [...]

**13** [...] I am struck silent, for what shall I speak that is not already known [...]

**14** [...] and what shall I declare that has not been told? All things [...]

**15** [...] are inscribed before You with the stylus of remembrance for all the appointed times [...]

**16** [...] of eternity, and the cycles of the years everlasting [...]

**17** [...] in all their appointed seasons, and they shall not be concealed [...]

**18** [...] from before You. How shall a mortal recount his transgression? [...]

**19** [...] and how shall he plead concerning his iniquity? [...]

**20** [...] and how shall he answer to righteous judgment? [...]

**21** [...] To You, O God of knowledge, belong all the works of righteousness [...]

**22** [...] and the counsel of truth; but to the children of mortals belongs the service of iniquity [...]

**23** [...] and the works of deceit. You created breath for the tongue [...]

**24** [...] and You know its words, and You ordained the fruit of the lips [...]

**25** [...] before they came to be. And You set words upon a measuring line [...]

**26** [...] and the utterance of the breath of the lips by measure [...]

**27** [...] and You bring forth sounds according to their mysteries [...]

**28** [...] and the outpourings of breath according to their reckoning, to make known [...]

**29** [...] Your glory and to recount Your wonders [...]

**30** [...] but Your mercies [...] have sustained me through all these things [...]

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 25 is very fragmentary. The physical-collapse lament (25:1-4) employs somatic imagery characteristic of the Hodayot's confessional style: heart, bones, flesh, knees all participate in the speaker's distress. The "stylus of remembrance" (25:15) reflects the deterministic theology of Qumran — all events are pre-inscribed. Recovery comes solely through divine mercy (25:30).*
